channel.title: Blockfront
channel.description: Blockfront reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, regulation, security incidents, funding rounds and network upgrades.

item.title: BaseSwap: When to Swap Tokens and When to Add Liquidity
item.description: A swap exchanges one token for another; a liquidity pool deposit supports future trades and may earn fees, with different costs and risks for each choice.

item.title: Mesh and Visa link wallet balances to 175 million merchants
item.description: Mesh will let participating wallet users pay online and in stores from crypto or stablecoin balances through Visa, with rollout details pending and no cash-out first.

item.title: Manta bridge transfers: why they wait and which route fits
item.description: A Manta bridge transfer can wait on wallet confirmation, cross-chain processing or a withdrawal step; check its stage before choosing a faster route.

item.title: Across users can skip repeat token approvals with a standing allowance
item.description: Across users can skip repeat approvals when a token allowance still covers the next bridge; changing the origin token, chain or spender can require a new one.

item.title: Mesh and Visa link crypto wallets to 175 million merchants
item.description: Mesh and Visa will let participating wallet users pay from crypto, stablecoin or fiat balances at Visa merchants, with rollout details still to come.

item.title: JPMorgan brings JPM Coin to Ethereum for institutional clients
item.description: JPMorgan has brought its dollar deposit token to Ethereum, adding a second public-chain option for institutional transfers and expanding access to onchain liquidity.

item.title: Tether joins AIsa seed extension as funding tops $9 million
item.description: Tether Capital and HIVEN joined AIsa’s seed extension, lifting total funding above $9 million as the company builds payment tools for enterprise AI agents.

item.title: Ledger says CryptoBilis devices hid LTE chips that stole recovery phrases
item.description: Ledger says hidden LTE implants in devices sold by CryptoBilis captured wallet recovery phrases during setup; the company is reviewing reseller controls.

item.title: Ledger reviews sales controls after $93 million wallet theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing sales and anti-tampering controls after modified wallets tied to reseller CryptoBilis helped drain an estimated $93 million in crypto.

item.title: Ledger Reviews Wallet Sales After $90 Million Crypto Theft
item.description: Ledger halted reseller sales across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong after implanted wallets exposed recovery phrases, prompting a review of its sales and anti-tampering controls.

item.title: Ledger confirms implant; CryptoBilis drain estimate tops $86M
item.description: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized implant in a drained device linked to CryptoBilis, while on-chain estimates put losses above $86 million and the total remains unverified.

item.title: Three checks to reduce allowance races in bridge wallets
item.description: Three checks—spender, amount and transaction order—help bridge users limit token approvals and avoid replacing a live allowance before it is spent on the source chain.

item.title: Check the Destination Before Your First Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: Check the destination network, token contract, fees and required gas before a first cross-chain swap; the displayed token name is not enough to confirm receipt.

item.title: Why a Bridged Token Can Take Longer to Arrive
item.description: Bridge arrival time depends on source-chain finality, bridge verification and destination execution; check each status before retrying or contacting support.

item.title: Prepare a Wallet for a Cross-Chain Governance Payment
item.description: Prepare the source wallet with the required asset and gas, then verify the destination chain, governance address, memo and receipt before sending a cross-chain payment.

item.title: How to Compare Both Records of a Crypto Bridge Transfer
item.description: Compare the source deposit with the destination fill using the shared deposit ID, recipient, tokens and amounts; a wallet balance alone cannot prove a bridge transfer completed.

item.title: Moving Liquidity When Rewards Shift Chains
item.description: When incentives move chains, liquidity providers must unwind the old position, bridge assets and rebuild on the new network after comparing net costs and risks.

item.title: Bridge First or One Route? How to Choose a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: Bridge first gives you control over the destination asset and swap; a one-route cross-chain trade cuts steps but can hide fees, timing and recovery.

item.title: Save These Details Before Contacting Cross-Chain Support
item.description: A useful cross-chain support record connects the source transaction to its destination, with chain names, token details, route, status and evidence saved together.

item.title: Why fast block times do not make every crypto swap instant
item.description: Block time measures how often a chain adds blocks, not how long a swap takes. Learn what causes delays and what to check before approving a transaction.
